capabilities: Pull AI-analyzed YouTube notes from the StackTube API on a schedule or on demand
Write Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter (video_id, channel, title, video_url, tags)
Avoid duplicate notes by identifying each video by video_id and resuming after restart
Capture a video frame at a timestamp and embed it in the note's frame slot
Show sync status and last-sync time via ribbon icon and status bar
extras: All video analysis runs on StackTube's servers; the plugin only fetches and writes files. A 'plan' is shown on connection test, suggesting a freemium service. Setup instructions include one Korean-language label (연결 테스트 / Test connection). Beta install via BRAT is available alongside a pending community-plugins listing.
motivation: The author's stated idea is that 'Videos stream by. Knowledge should stack up.' — turning transient video watching into accumulated, owned notes.
problem: Watching YouTube produces knowledge that streams by and is lost; Obsidian has no built-in way to turn monitored channels' videos into structured, searchable notes.

relations.evidence: This plugin is a thin client: all analysis happens on the StackTube server.
runs each new video through an AI pipeline (Gemini + Claude)

summary: Sync client that pulls AI-structured YouTube video notes from the StackTube service into the vault as Markdown files.
